Text: $SNDK $MU NAND flash to become the next major supply bottleneck and potentially experience the strongest price increases in 2027. Memory Supply Remains Tight BMO analyst Harsh Kumar expects the memory industry to remain undersupplied as AI demand increases across DRAM, high-bandwidth memory and NAND. Kumar said one distributor estimated demand at roughly three times available supply. He expects supply and demand to remain out of balance throughout 2027 and potentially into part of 2028. Rising HBM production is also tightening conventional DRAM availability because HBM requires roughly three times the die area, Kumar said. At the same time, agentic AI applications are increasing demand for server DRAM such as DDR5. Kumar expects NAND flash to become the next major supply bottleneck and potentially experience the strongest price increases next year.
